message.content: REST typically uses HTTP with JSON payloads and relies on resource-based URIs; it lacks a strict schema, often requiring clients to handle versioning manually. GraphQL operates over HTTP (usually POST) but enforces a strongly typed schema defined in SDL (Schema Definition Language), allowing clients to request exact data fields in a single query. gRPC uses HTTP/2 as its transport protocol and relies on Protocol Buffers (Protobuf) for a strictly typed, binary schema, enabling high-performance, bidirectional streaming between services. While REST is flexible and widely adopted for public APIs, GraphQL offers precise data fetching, and gRPC provides superior efficiency for internal microservices communication.
